questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an English speaking country (in Europe). That it was not in the capital city, as I wanted to get a better sense of the local culture and environment. Seemed like a good university for my studying and also seemed like a good environment for global students and exchange students. That it was possible to live in a student accomodation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing time in my time abroad. Met so many nice people, the courses were interesting and challenging and I still felt like I had time to really see the most of the country while staying there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Not everything was easy to locate. The website for the University is very big and certain things were just difficult to find. I did get mails to help me through the beginning but there were still some unanswered questions that I had difficulties finding. 
Also, I was dissappointed to learn only a few days before, that they had a week of orientation for exchange students before the semester started. Because I had not heard or read anything about this, I was not able to attend any of these events unfortunately.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much to be honest. It could have been a bit better. In my first week I was really confused about my schedule, how the university webportal worked and even where to go for help about these things. People were friendly though, and when I finally got hold of the right person I got help. But administratively things went a bit slow, which made me miss out on some things in the first week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of information had to be given obviously, and I did receive a great deal of such, but there were still lack of information that I would have wanted and needed when arriving. Especially considering my schedule.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Only two options were available both close to the city centre.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No option for meal plans, but we had a nice kitchen at the accomodation and therefore nice cooking facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is not cheap, and obviously one should prepare to live with other people and share a kitchen and common room. But you avoid the hastle of trying to find a place on your own, once you wanted a student accomodation you will get it and everything went quite smoothly with this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have been nice to have the option of chosing a bit more of the available accomodations. Unfortunately that was not possible for me, either because I was an erasmus student or because I only stayed for the spring semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite easy, just needed to go to the office at a chosen time. However the information about the registration proces I received a bit late.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I booked a time slot and arrived at the registration office. From there everything went quite smoothly and was assisted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: People.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The classes that I have requested beforehand and had been preapproved from home were the classes I got. So everything went quite smoothly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Book a time slot in advance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting and challenging courses, I really enjoyed the teaching structure of weekly seminars with professors as I am not too used to this at home. Also I had good time to prepare for my courses each week which was nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As I was a MA student, I had MA level courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
More seminar structure with the professor, as I am used to more lectures and then class teaching with more of a teaching instructor. Because the seminars ran with fewer students in the room, I really enjoyed the way that you get to talk a lot about the subject matter and get the hints and clarifications from the professor as well. 
The level of education was however pretty much the same and both types of teaching do encourage to discussion and making up ones own oppinion (which is important in my field of study)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Freedom POL6619. About the concept of freedom in political theory (leaning towards political philosophy)
Feminist and Decolonizing Approaches to International Relations- bodies, coloniality, knowledge POL6611. Title is selfexplanatory for the course.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Both courses were quite nice, but I guess it depends what ones interests are. I personally really enjoyed the Freedom course, as I liked the political philosophy aspect of it. However if one is interested in feminism/decolonisation and International Relations that course was quite interesting as well.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any unexpected costs. However transportation costs may vary as some people lived further away from university buildings than I did. However in most people just walk everywhere instead of using public transportation or such.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had expected food prices to be a bit less actually, but in reality they were quite similar to danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was maybe the best part about my stay. The university has so many societies and opportunities to play sports, share your interests and just meet new people. Quite the bee's knees!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Societies. And a bunch load of them. There are societies for all kinds and all types of interests. Different sports societies, walking society (for hiking), dancing societies, music societies, baking society, even tea society and duck society were a thing!
Also, the students union is great and one if not the best in the country. University parties take place in the union multiple times a week.
Furthermore there are also small activities done by global campus and the residence life team (some better than others though).
Another quite nice thing is the "Give it a go" - concept, where one can find tours and trips to different cities and activities often in the weekend. It's a nice and easy way to get to do some sightseeing while there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a society! There are so many, so should be possible to find something to like, it is great fun and just a perfect way to meet new people. I also found socities a good way to interact more with the brits and local students, whereas it otherwise is quite common for exchange students to hang out with other exvhange students (also nice, but to get to meet local people are a nice way to get a better sense of the culture your in)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There is the Give it a go, that often has trips to different cities on the weekends.
I travelled a lot (with my flatmates and other people I had met) to different cities or towns around England, which was a nice way of experiencing the country.
Also, the Peaks district! A national park just next to Sheffield, where so many go on hikes and enjoy nature, so beautiful - and a must! 
Otherwise Sheffield has a lot of nice cafés and parks to visit and enjoy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy I would say. The first couple of weeks can be quite overwhelming though, and it's okay to need some time to settle in. However if one is comfortable with english things settle themselves quite easily to be honest. Just give it a little time and remember to talk with people. Also, try to go on trips or excursions to see different parts of the country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think the best way is to get involved with societies. Depending on the courses one takes, it is also possible to get to know people through group work and such.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The way the brits don't know how to insulate their housing. So cold... 
Also, the food is not the best, but if you can settle for a pint and a pie, all will be fine.
oh and also, Sheffield is really hilly. As in REALLY hilly, one's legs will be strong:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The university culture, students union and societies were just so nice. Sheffield definitely feels like a student city which I quite enjoyed. I also actually enjoyed that most people just walked everywhere. Definitely got my average stepcount up!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to join as many activities, excursions and societies as is possible with your time.
Get to know people, and if you are in doubt about anything ask - Brits wanna help but won't always reach out by themselves, needs to be asked.
The studies are important, but try to make the most of your stay! It is once in a life time, sometimes I would chose an excursion over the weekly reading (oops!)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is nice to have a students accomodation.
Be patient with the administration things and ask for help in the students union if any worries of any kind comes up.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Friends, people, new culture. Actually quite nice to get to speak so much english for a longer period of time.
Traveling a lot while there was also quite nice.
Also, I stayed for about a month after the semester had ended because I continues to have my accomodation available. In that time I really tried to make the most of my stay, travelled a lot, and tried to go to many different places in Sheffield to exerience the city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first two weeks. Just seemed very overwhelming, and I struggled with not having my schedule and such. Hang in there:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
